subject: Post-renewal usage spike — reconciliation and one-time bridge charge
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@neonhealth.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: NeonHealth Billing <finance@neonhealth.io>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:14:00Z
Subject: Unexpected spike after renewal — request for reconciliation

Hi Monica,

We closed our renewal with Redwood on 2027-05-01 (thanks again) but saw a ~3.8x jump in inference hours during the first billing period that looks retroactive to work done in early April. Finance flagged the invoice we received on 2027-05-02 and asked for a breakdown before they process payment.

Can you help reconcile the spike? Specifically we need: a per-day/hour consumption export, a mapping to model/route tags, and any recommended path for a one-time bridge charge or credit while we sort internal tagging. I've attached the billing notice we received.

Best,
Olivia
Billing Ops — NeonHealth
attachments: billing_notice_may02.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@neonhealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike after renewal — request for reconciliation

Hi Olivia — thanks for flagging and sorry for the surprise. We're pulling the daily consumption export now and will run a quick attribution by service/route.

Initial thought: two possibilities we see in similar cases — (1) customer-side tagging changes that retroactively route requests to a higher-throughput model variant, or (2) a rollout where a canary accidentally received more traffic after the term change. Either way we can:
- Produce a CSV with per-day, model, route, and token counts (attached)
- Propose a split remediation: a one-time bridge charge that covers documented excess, plus a discretionary credit if we find Redwood-side misrouting.

I'll send the export and a proposed credit calc within 48 hours. If finance needs an immediate stopgap, we can issue a temporary invoice hold while we reconcile.

--
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference

From: NeonHealth Billing <finance@neonhealth.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T08:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike after renewal — request for reconciliation

Thanks Monica — we've attached our internal telemetry export (metrics_team_usage_may.csv) and the PO reference (PO-99822). We can sign off on an interim bridge charge if it's clearly scoped and itemized; otherwise billing will hold the invoice until reconciliation is complete.

Olivia (Finance)
attachments: metrics_team_usage_may.csv, PO-99822.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: NeonHealth Billing <finance@neonhealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike after renewal — request for reconciliation

Team — attached is the per-day export we generated from Redwood (usage_report_May2027.csv) plus a preliminary credit worksheet (proposed_credit_calc.xlsx). Highlights: 
- The bulk of the excess (~72%) maps to a route tag "/v1/realtime/async-preview" that was migrated during the renewal cutover.
- There is a ~18% delta we can attribute to NeonHealth-side batch jobs (timestamp mismatch).
- Proposed remediation: one-time bridge charge of $18,600 for clearly-documented excess across the renewal boundary, plus a discretionary goodwill credit of $4,000 to cover the tagging ambiguity while you finish internal reconciliation.

Requesting internal approval from finance to: (A) authorize the $18.6k invoice and (B) apply the $4k credit as a line-item (net ~$14.6k charged). If finance prefers, we can amortize the $4k credit across the remaining 7 months of the term instead of applying upfront.

--
Monica
attachments: usage_report_May2027.csv, proposed_credit_calc.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-06T10:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Post-renewal usage spike — reconciliation and one-time bridge charge

Monica — I reviewed the worksheet and the usage export. Approve the remediation plan with one change: convert the $4k discretionary credit into a 6-month amortized credit (we'll show as a line item but invoice the net now and post a recurring negative line on next six invoices to claw back). Rationale: keeps revenue tidy for month close while giving the customer smoothing.

Ben Carter
Head of Billing Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@neonhealth.io>, NeonHealth Billing <finance@neonhealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-07T16:02:00Z
Subject: Final: reconciled invoice and payment instructions (PO-99822)

Hi Olivia — thanks for sending the telemetry. Per Ben's approval we've finalized the approach:
- One-time bridge charge: $18,600 (covers documented excess during renewal boundary).
- Amortized credit: $4,000 split across 6 months (negative recurring line on invoices).
- Net immediate invoice: $14,600.

I've attached the corrected invoice (corrected_invoice_20270507.pdf) and included your PO reference on line 1. Payment terms: Net 30 from invoice date. If you prefer we can instead mark the one-time charge to the next billing cycle and net it against prepayments — let us know.

Next steps:
- Olivia/Finance: confirm acceptance and we'll mark the invoice final.
- Redwood: we'll monitor the /v1/realtime/async-preview routing and follow up if we find any infra-side misconfig that contributed.

Thanks — appreciate the quick coordination.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference
attachments: corrected_invoice_20270507.pdf
